newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. approves Physician Health Services rate cut.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. approves Physician Health Services rate cut.

text.p: The New York State Insurance Department said Tuesday Physician Health Services of New York has been granted its requested 19.7 percent rate decrease on the in-network portion of its PHS/Guardian Healthcare Solutions point-of-service contract.
The rate change is effective retroactive to July 1 and affects the health maintenance organization's 44,000 members who have the point-of-service product, the department said.

However, because Guardian Life Insurance Co of America, which provides the out-of-network portion of the contract, implemented a rate increase on July 1, the actual net result for policyholders with the point-of-service product is an average 6.2 percent increase.
Guardian Life's rate increase did not require the department's prior approval, it noted.

It said the primary reason the HMO requested a rate decrease was to reallocate the premium rates on its point-of-service contract to reflect actual use of benefits. The rate decrease for the in-network portion written by Physician Health Services and the rate increase for the out-of-network portion written by Guardian is in recognition of the greater use of the out-of-network benefits.
